newsitem.title: MOROCCO: MOROCCO DELISTS SEC PORTFOLIO FIRM FROM BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: MOROCCO DELISTS SEC PORTFOLIO FIRM FROM BOURSE.

text.p: Morocco reduced the number of listed companies on the Casablanca stock exchange to 48 after the delisting of small portfolio firm Societe Epargne Croissance (SEC), a bourse official said on Friday.
"SEC firm, which was not traded for months and failed to comply with the bourse's transparency rules, was delisted this week," the official told Reuters.
The firm, which belongs to Al-Amane insurance group, was traded earlier this year at up to 246 dirhams, he said.
It has no Reuters Identification Code.
The Casablanca stock exchange had 49 listed stocks among them five portfolio companies, including SEC firm.

With a market capitalisation of 117 billion dirhams ($11.7 billion), the bourse is undergoing a deep financial reform launched by the authorities in 1993. This coincided with the privatisation of 114 companies, the broker said.

To improve its image abroad and attract more investors to the bourse, Morocco is pushing for strict respect of transparency rules on the market after it delisted more than 20 firms since 1993, he added.
One of the oldest stock echanges in Africa, the Casablanca bourse was established in 1929 when Morocco was a French protectorate.
